key_reasons.assessment: Entity roles enter through both contextual marked H and explicit R. A natural entity-pair change can alter token states, attention scores and signed utilities simultaneously. Fixed-H/R interventions identify sensitivity of the explicit path; interpreting them as naturally relabeled queries would require an additional independently observed premise.

The relevant pair margin is m_ab = b_a - b_b + sum_t(alpha_at*u_at) - sum_t(alpha_bt*u_bt). Signed, input-dependent utilities and separate class normalizations prevent overlap growth or attention interaction alone from determining margin improvement. Correct classification additionally requires every competing-class margin to satisfy the decision rule.

The supplied classical constructions defeat the proposed interaction diagnostic at two levels: role-only scoring with changing utilities produces I=1/3, and additive content-plus-role log-odds with fixed utilities produces I=-1/30. Fixed-value replay therefore does not isolate scorer-internal interaction, and output interaction supplies no quantum-discriminating prediction.

Generic Born overlap, realification, normalization, finite differences and label-wise attention already collide with supplied known mechanisms or tools. The native circuit, bounded angle map and per-token floor specify an implementation, but the packet establishes no distinct task consequence from those choices. Previously stopped families supply no qualified route to reopen.

Existing evidence supports fixed-model context weight-to-value alignment and Macro utility over uniform under the stated seed assumptions. It establishes neither superiority nor equivalence against matched alternatives, and neither quantum attribution nor mediation of total utility. The seven selected cases provide exploratory traces with no population decision guarantee.

No independently measured semantic structure currently anchors a different class-margin prediction. Supplying an inverse-label law, independent-view condition or quantum-realizable target rule would introduce an unsupported premise. A changed mechanism would require new L4 evidence.
